newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ford dealer sees Japan sales of 28,000 cars in '97.
newsitem.headline: Ford dealer sees Japan sales of 28,000 cars in '97.

text.p: Autorama Inc, the sole Japanese dealer for Ford Motor Co cars, forecasts sales of 28,000 Ford cars in Japan in 1997, Keiji Matsuda, general manager in charge of Japanese sales, said on Tuesday.
Mazda Motor Corp and Ford Motor each have a 45.1 percent stake in Autorama. Ford owns 33.4 percent of Mazda.
Ford sales in Japan are likely to hit 22,000 cars in 1996, up from an actual 20,840 in 1995, Matsuda said. The sales figures include sales of Ford cars made by Mazda.
Early this year, the company forecast sales of 35,000 cars in Japan in 1996.

Autorama on Tuesday launched a completely remodelled Mondeo sedan and station wagon, and a partially remodelled Explorer heavy sport-utility vehicle in Japan. Its monthly sales targets are 1,000 Mondeos and 500 Explorers.
"Demand for these new models in the initial period could be bigger than the target," Matsuda said.
The local sales price will start at 1.795 million yen for the Mondeo sedan, 2.245 million yen for the station wagon, and 2.795 million yen for the Explorer.
